stem: A hospital's HCAHPS results show a sustained decline in patient ratings of communication with nurses. Which nursing response best reflects performance-improvement practice?

options.A: Participate in reviewing the communication data, implement an evidence-based improvement strategy, and evaluate whether patient-care results improve
options.B: Ignore the results because patient-experience data are not relevant to quality improvement
options.C: Change the medical record documentation so the survey scores appear more favorable
options.D: Survey only patients expected to give positive ratings before deciding whether improvement is needed

rationale: CMS describes HCAHPS as a national standardized survey of patients' perspectives of hospital care and includes communication with nurses among the measured domains. NCSBN's 2026 test plan places participation in performance-improvement projects, use of research and other references for improvement actions, and evaluation of the impact of improvement measures within Management of Care. Therefore the nurse should use the identified care issue as quality-improvement data, participate in an evidence-based intervention, and evaluate its effect. A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Use patient-experience quality data such as HCAHPS nurse-communication results to participate in evidence-based performance improvement and evaluate the impact on client care.
source_version_date: Current CMS webpage accessed 2026-08-17; survey content updated beginning 2025
source_locator: Overview/About the survey: HCAHPS is a national, standardized, publicly reported survey of patients' perspectives of hospital care and captures patient experience of communication with nurses and other hospital-care domains
source_claim_supported: HCAHPS provides standardized patient-experience data, including communication with nurses, that can identify a care-quality issue for performance-improvement work.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26: participate in performance improvement projects and quality improvement processes; report identified client-care issues; utilize research/references for performance-improvement actions; evaluate impact of performance-improvement measures on client care and resource use
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement / use of patient-experience data
correction_summary: Replaced low-value recall of the HCAHPS post-discharge administration window with an applied NCLEX-relevant performance-improvement item using HCAHPS nurse-communication data. The revised item tests the RN's quality-improvement role rather than survey logistics.
audit_findings: A directly matches NCSBN performance-improvement activities and uses a CMS-defined HCAHPS domain. B incorrectly dismisses standardized quality data. C is unethical and does not improve care. D introduces biased selective surveying rather than responding to existing standardized results. No timing window or survey methodology detail is needed for the construct. Independent second pass found one best answer, no cueing, and a direct Management of Care mapping.
audit_reviewer: GPT-5.6 Sol Rule 1 — item-by-item semantic audit
final_reaudit_scope: current CMS HCAHPS content; NCSBN 2026 performance-improvement locator; claim-by-claim; A-D distractor audit; ambiguity/second-answer/cueing; independent adversarial second pass
